applicability_by_reference: Boeing Alert Service Bulletin 737–53A1217, Revision 1, dated September 8, 2022
compliance_time: At the applicable times specified in Tables 3 through 6 of Boeing Alert Service Bulletin 737–53A1217, Revision 1, dated September 8, 2022
required_action: Perform repetitive internal and external detailed inspections, low frequency eddy current (LFEC), and medium frequency eddy current (MFEC) inspections for cracks of the skin repair of S–17 at STA 360 to STA 380 and STA 888 to STA 907, left and right sides of the airplane, with corrective actions including repair as necessary.
extraction_notes: This is a Notice of Proposed Rulemaking (NPRM), not a final AD. The AD number is inferred from the docket and project identifier information. The applicability is limited to Group 1 through 3, Configuration 3 airplanes as identified in Boeing Alert Service Bulletin 737–53A1217. The document indicates this is a proposed rule with a comment due date of July 10, 2023.

compliance_time: Within 30 days after the effective date of this AD for inspection; replacement times vary by manufacturing date: before further flight or within 15 years since date of manufacture (whichever occurs later) for 2008 or earlier; within 12 months for 2009-2010; within 24 months for 2011-2013; before exceeding 10 years since date of manufacture or within 24 months (whichever occurs later) for 2014 or later
required_action: Inspect passenger chemical oxygen generators (part numbers 117080-02, 117080-03, 117080-04) to determine date of manufacture within 30 days. Replace affected generators with serviceable units according to manufacturing date-based compliance times. Prohibit installation of non-serviceable passenger chemical oxygen generators.

applicability_by_reference: Boeing Special Attention Requirements Bulletin 737–53–1399 RB, Revision 1, dated March 14, 2023
compliance_time: At the applicable times specified in the Compliance paragraph of Boeing Special Attention Requirements Bulletin 737–53–1399 RB, Revision 1, dated March 14, 2023
required_action: Perform general visual inspection for any repair, buckle, wrinkle, bulge, and cracking at skin lap splices at stringers S–4, S–14, and S–24; perform repetitive detailed inspections for buckling, wrinkling, or bulging at unrepaired areas of affected lap splices and repair; perform repetitive detailed, high frequency eddy current, and ultrasonic inspections for cracking at affected locations and repair; and perform alternative inspections and on-condition actions as specified in Boeing Special Attention Requirements Bulletin 737–53–1399 RB, Revision 1, dated March 14, 2023.
extraction_notes: The AD references Boeing Special Attention Requirements Bulletin 737–53–1399 RB, Revision 1, dated March 14, 2023 for specific compliance times and detailed accomplishment instructions. The Related Service Information section indicates that S–4R applies only to 737–800 Boeing Converted Freighter airplanes, while S–24R applies only to 737–600, –700, –700C, –800, –900, and –900ER series airplanes. However, the applicability section (c)(1) states the AD applies to all six models listed. The specific applicability by stringer location is defined in the referenced service bulletin.

applicability_by_reference: Boeing Alert Service Bulletin 737–53A1217, Revision 1, dated September 8, 2022
compliance_time: At the applicable times specified in Tables 3 through 6 of paragraph 1.E., "Compliance," of Boeing Alert Service Bulletin 737–53A1217, Revision 1, dated September 8, 2022
required_action: Perform repetitive internal and external detailed inspections, low frequency eddy current (LFEC) inspections, and medium frequency eddy current (MFEC) inspections for cracks of the skin repair at stringer S–17, station 360 to 380 and station 888 to 907, left and right sides. Perform corrective actions including repair if necessary.
extraction_notes: The AD applies to Group 1 through 3, Configuration 3 airplanes as identified in the referenced service bulletin. Specific serial number ranges are not provided in the AD text itself; applicability is defined by reference to the service bulletin.

applicability_by_reference: Boeing Alert Requirements Bulletin 737–25A1873 RB, dated August 25, 2023; Boeing Alert Requirements Bulletin 737–25A1876 RB, dated September 1, 2023
compliance_time: As specified in Boeing Alert Requirements Bulletin 737–25A1873 RB (for 737-300 and -400) or Boeing Alert Requirements Bulletin 737–25A1876 RB (for 737-800), with compliance times measured from the effective date of this AD
required_action: Inspect certain galleys to determine part numbers, inspect for existing galley modification placard and marking, and replace wire bundle spiral wrap sleeving as applicable. Prohibit installation of affected galley wire bundle spiral wrap made of polyethylene with self-wrapping sleeve.
extraction_notes: This is a Proposed Rule (NPRM) dated June 24, 2024. The AD number is derived from the FR Doc. number (2024–13490) and the publication date. The applicability is defined by reference to two separate Boeing Alert Requirements Bulletins, which apply to different airplane models. Compliance times are specified in those referenced documents and measured from the effective date of the AD.

applicability_by_reference: Boeing 737–800BCF Airworthiness Limitations, D140A006, Revision L, dated April 1, 2021
compliance_time: Before the airplane accumulates 17,000 total flight cycles, or within 5,000 flight cycles after July 17, 2019, or within 12 months after the effective date of this AD, or within 1,000 flight cycles after the effective date of this AD, whichever occurs last
required_action: Perform an ultrasonic inspection of the skin under the drag link assembly for cracks and accomplish applicable on-condition actions including repairs using approved methods.
extraction_notes: This is a proposed rule (NPRM), not yet final. The AD number format appears non-standard for FAA (typically YYYY-NN-NN). Based on the Federal Register document date (September 25, 2024) and the project identifier AD-2023-00537-T, the actual AD number when finalized may differ. The applicability is limited to Model 737-800 series airplanes converted to freighter configuration using Boeing Drawing 800A0003 before April 1, 2021, and identified as Group A in the referenced Airworthiness Limitations document. The compliance time has multiple conditions with "whichever occurs last" logic. This AD replaces the initial ultrasonic inspections required by paragraph (g) of AD 2019-11-06 for these specific aircraft only.

applicability_by_reference: Boeing Alert Requirements Bulletin 747–53A2912 RB, dated April 5, 2024
compliance_time: As specified in Boeing Alert Requirements Bulletin 747–53A2912 RB, dated April 5, 2024
required_action: Perform inspections and corrective actions to detect and correct cracking of the upper fastener row of the fuselage skin lap splice between STAs 1350 and 1480 at stringers S–23L and S–23R, in accordance with Boeing Alert Requirements Bulletin 747–53A2912 RB, dated April 5, 2024.

applicability_by_reference: Boeing 737-800BCF Airworthiness Limitations, D140A006, Revision L, dated April 1, 2021 (Section 5.2.1 identifies Group A airplanes)
compliance_time: At the compliance time specified in paragraph (g)(1)(i), (ii), (iii), or (iv), whichever occurs last: before the airplane accumulates 17,000 total flight cycles, or within 5,000 flight cycles after July 17, 2019, or within 12 months after the effective date of this AD, or within 1,000 flight cycles after the effective date of this AD. For Group 1 Configuration 1, 3, or 4: before 30,000 total flight cycles, or within 5,000 flight cycles after July 17, 2019, or within 12 months after the effective date, or within 1,000 flight cycles after the effective date.
required_action: Perform an ultrasonic inspection of the skin under the drag link assembly (Part 2) or repair tripler under the drag link assembly (Part 6) in accordance with Boeing Alert Service Bulletin 737-53A1368, dated February 27, 2018, and do all applicable on-condition actions including repairs as approved.
extraction_notes: Applicability is limited to Model 737-800 series airplanes converted to freighter configuration using Boeing Drawing 800A0003 before April 1, 2021, and identified as Group A in the referenced Airworthiness Limitations document. The AD specifies different inspection requirements based on configuration groups (Group 1 Configurations 2, 3, 4, 5 or Group 5 vs. Group 1 Configurations 1, 3, 4). Serial numbers are not specified in the AD itself; applicability is defined by reference to the Airworthiness Limitations document.

compliance_time: Within 4 months after the effective date of this AD
required_action: Replace lavatory bifold door latches with part numbers SC1L500031–3/20218–3, SC1L500031–4/20218–4, SC1L500031–5/20218–5/20218–7, or SC1L500031–6/20218–6/20218–8 with improved latches having part numbers SC1L500031–9/20218–9 or SC1L500031–10/20218–10. Prohibit installation of the affected parts.
extraction_notes: This is a Notice of Proposed Rulemaking (NPRM) dated April 11, 2025. The AD number is not yet assigned in the document; the project identifier is AD–2024–00208–T. The actual AD number format (YYYY-NN-NN) cannot be determined from this NPRM text. The applicability is limited to airplanes with specific lavatory bifold door latch part numbers as listed in section (c). No serial number ranges are specified in the applicability section.

applicability_by_reference: European Union Aviation Safety Agency AD 2025-0025, dated January 23, 2025
compliance_time: As specified in EASA AD 2025-0025, with effective date of this AD used where EASA AD refers to its effective date
required_action: Adjust the cargo swing emergency release control in accordance with EASA AD 2025-0025, with clarifications that distance 'B' is between the ball end and manual release lever, and distance 'C' is between the ball end and dropping control.
extraction_notes: This is an FAA AD that adopts EASA AD 2025-0025 by reference. The AD number in the FAA document is not explicitly stated in the format YYYY-NN-NN; it references EASA AD 2025-0025. The FAA AD number should be derived from the docket (FAA-2025-1363) and project identifier (MCAI-2025-00098-R), but the actual FAA AD number is not clearly printed. Based on the structure, this appears to be an adoption of the EASA AD. The extraction uses the EASA AD number as the reference since that is what is incorporated by reference.

applicability_by_reference: Airbus Alert Operators Transmission (AOT) A32N033-24 Revision 02 or Revision 03; Triumph Service Bulletin 114122-32-108
compliance_time: For Group 1 aeroplanes with affected part 1: within 8 days or 5 flight cycles (whichever occurs later) from last inspection or before next flight after 04 August 2025, then at intervals not exceeding 8 days or 5 FC. For affected part 2: within 15 days after 04 August 2025, then at intervals not exceeding 8 days or 5 FC. Replacement of affected part 1 within 12 months after 22 November 2024; affected part 2 within 18 months after 04 August 2025. From 04 August 2025, do not install any affected part on any aeroplane.
required_action: Inspect each affected main landing gear (MLG) door actuator (P/N 114122015 with specific serial numbers listed in AOT A32N033-24) for jamming or inability to open. If discrepancies are detected, replace the affected part with a serviceable part before next flight. Alternatively, accomplish X-ray inspection per VSB Revision 01 or AOT Revision 03 to terminate repetitive inspections. Do not install any affected parts on any aeroplane from 04 August 2025 onwards.
extraction_notes: This is Revision 2 of AD 2025-0158. The affected parts are specifically defined by serial numbers listed in Appendix 1 Lists A and B of the AOT, which is referenced as the authoritative source. The AD applies to all MSN of the listed aircraft models. Group 1 aeroplanes have affected parts installed; Group 2 do not. The X-ray inspection method (paragraph 8) provides an acceptable alternative to replacement for terminating repetitive inspections.

compliance_time: Before exceeding the threshold and thereafter at intervals as defined in Table 1, depending on aeroplane group and zone. Thresholds range from 19,500 flight cycles since first flight or last repair to 3 months after 10 November 2025, with inspection intervals of 500, 1000, or 2000 flight cycles depending on group and zone.
required_action: Accomplish Special Detailed Inspection (SDI) of each zone of the 80VU rack attachments in accordance with Airbus Service Bulletin A320-25-1BKJ Revision 04 or A320-25-1CJH Revision 01, as applicable. If discrepancies are detected, accomplish applicable corrective actions within the compliance time specified in the SB. Report inspection results to Airbus within 90 days after each SDI or after 10 November 2025, whichever occurs later.
extraction_notes: This is Revision 01 of AD 2025-0237, issued as a correction on 24 June 2026 (effective 30 June 2026). The original issue was 10 November 2025. The AD applies to all manufacturer serial numbers. Applicability is complex and depends on aeroplane configuration (CEO vs NEO) and modification status, organized into 5 groups with different inspection thresholds and intervals for three zones (A, B, C). The AD references two service bulletins: A320-25-1BKJ Revision 04 for CEO aeroplanes and A320-25-1CJH Revision 01 for NEO aeroplanes. The compliance time is expressed in flight cycles with multiple threshold conditions that vary by group and zone.

compliance_time: Within 6 months after 06 November 2025 for replacement of affected parts with serial numbers listed in Appendix 1; within 24 months after 06 November 2025 for inspection of affected parts with serial numbers not listed in Appendix 1; from the effective date of this AD, affected parts may be installed provided they pass inspection concurrently with installation
required_action: Replace fire panels with affected part numbers and serial numbers listed in Appendix 1 within 6 months; inspect fire panels with affected part numbers but serial numbers not listed in Appendix 1 within 24 months; do not install affected parts with serial numbers listed in Appendix 1 unless repaired and reinspected as applicable; all installations must be accompanied by inspection showing no damage in accordance with service bulletins.
extraction_notes: Serial ranges extracted from Appendix 1 for affected part numbers 330TS08Y, 335TS08Y00, 335TS08Y01, 700TS06Y11, and 700TS06Y12. The AD applies to all manufacturer serial numbers of the listed aircraft models, but specific actions are triggered only for affected parts with serial numbers listed in Appendix 1. The applicability_by_reference field is not used because the affected aircraft are explicitly listed by model variant. This is a revision (R1) of AD 2025-0274, which itself superseded earlier ADs 2025-0253 and 2025-0234.

applicability_by_reference: Safran Aerosystems Evacuation Vendor Service Bulletin A320 004-25-130
compliance_time: For Group 1 aeroplanes: within 36 months after 11 March 2026. For Group 2 aeroplanes: do not install affected slides after 11 March 2026.
required_action: Replace each affected evacuation slide with a serviceable slide in accordance with Airbus Service Bulletin A320-25-1CML or A320-25-1CMM. Do not install affected slides on any aeroplane.
extraction_notes: This is a revision (R1) of EASA AD 2026-0037. Applicability is complex: Group 1 aeroplanes have affected slides at specific door positions (FIN 7500MM, 7501MM, 7502MM, 7503MM) and must replace them within 36 months. Group 2 aeroplanes have no affected slides installed. Affected slides are identified by part number (D31516-XXX or D31517-XXX) and serial number ranges listed in Appendix 1. Affected hoses are also defined by part number and serial number. The AD allows for identification through maintenance records review. Serial number suffixes "RP" do not alter the identification as affected parts.

compliance_time: Within compliance time as identified in Table 1 (threshold A, B, C, D, E or F, whichever occurs later), then at intervals as defined in Table 2. Threshold A: before exceeding 21,100 flight cycles since first flight; Threshold B: within 17,300 FC since accomplishment of MSB; Threshold C: within 3,150 FC after first rework; Threshold D: within 12,400 FC after second or third rework; Threshold E: within 890 FC after last accomplishment of ALI task 531105-01-2; Threshold F: within 3,150 FC after last accomplishment of ALI task 531105-02-2. Intervals per Table 2 range from 2,400 to 5,200 FC depending on affected part configuration.
required_action: Accomplish repetitive High Frequency Eddy Current (HFEC) inspections of horizontal upper stiffeners of lateral window frame at fuselage Frame 4 (both RH and LH sides) in accordance with Airbus Service Bulletin A320-53-1544 or A320-53-1545. If discrepancies are detected, accomplish applicable corrective actions per the inspection SB before next flight.
extraction_notes: Applicability excludes aeroplanes on which Airbus modifications 165961, 162338, or 162339 were embodied in production. The compliance time is complex with multiple thresholds (A-F) and intervals that vary based on part configuration and maintenance history. Serial number ranges are not specified; all MSN are affected except those with specific modifications already embodied.

compliance_time: Within 4 months after the effective date for initial general visual inspection (GVI) of affected battery retaining rods, then at intervals not to exceed 4 months. Before next flight after hard landing or severe turbulence, accomplish GVI. Within 24 months after effective date, accomplish detailed inspection to identify manufacturer. Replacement of affected parts must be done before next flight if defects are found.
required_action: Accomplish repetitive general visual inspections (GVI) of battery retaining rods (Part Number D9241023700000) on Group 1 aeroplanes. Within 24 months, perform detailed inspection to identify manufacturer. Replace affected parts with serviceable parts if quality stamp shows "SA" manufacturer identification, or identify rods with applicable label if not "SA" marked. Replacement or reidentification constitutes terminating action for repetitive inspections.
extraction_notes: The AD defines two groups: Group 1 aeroplanes have affected parts installed; Group 2 aeroplanes do not. Affected parts are battery retaining rods with P/N D9241023700000 that were originally installed on battery support assemblies with "SA" quality marking or "SA" designation in supplier P/N, unless already identified with the applicable SB label. Serial number applicability is "all manufacturer serial numbers (MSN)" so no specific ranges are listed. Engine models are not applicable to this AD.

compliance_time: Initial inspection within compliance time as defined in Table 1 (for A318) or Table 2 (for A319, A320, A321) based on accumulated flight cycles and flight hours since first flight, ranging from 2,500 to 5,000 flight cycles or 5,000 to 10,000 flight hours after effective date depending on aircraft age; thereafter at intervals not to exceed 6,950 flight cycles or 13,900 flight hours, whichever occurs first
required_action: Accomplish repetitive rototest inspections of the forward pressure bulkhead hole C1 at Frame 35 (or Frame 35.8 for A321) at Stringer 30 on both left-hand and right-hand sides in accordance with the inspection service bulletin. If any crack is detected, contact Airbus for approved repair instructions before next flight. Modification of the affected areas in accordance with the modification service bulletin constitutes terminating action for the repetitive inspections.
extraction_notes: Applicability excludes: A318 aeroplanes with mod 39195 or SB A320-00-1219; A319 CEO with mods 28238, 28162, 28342; A319 NEO with mod 162338; A320 NEO with mod 162339; all aeroplanes with mod 174066. Compliance time is complex and depends on accumulated flight cycles/hours at effective date, with different thresholds for A318 versus A319/A320/A321. The AD references inspection SBs (A320-53-1532 or A320-53-1533) and modification SBs (A320-53-1534 or A320-53-1535) as applicable.

compliance_time: For Group 1 aeroplanes: before next flight after 29 November 2025. For Group 2 aeroplanes: from 29 November 2025, do not modify any aeroplane into a Group 1 aeroplane. AFM update required within 7 days after the effective date of this AD (22 July 2026).
required_action: Replace or modify each affected ELAC (ELAC B L104) with a serviceable ELAC (ELAC B L103+ or any subsequent eligible ELAC) in accordance with Airbus AOT or SB instructions. After modification, do not install an affected ELAC. Amend the AFM in accordance with Airbus FOT instructions.
extraction_notes: The AD defines two groups of aeroplanes with different compliance requirements. Group 1 aeroplanes had the affected configuration on 29 November 2025 (effective date of the superseded AD 2025-0268-E) and must replace/modify the ELAC before next flight after that date. Group 2 aeroplanes must not be modified into Group 1 configuration from 29 November 2025 onwards. The affected ELAC is specifically ELAC B L104 (P/N 3945129118 or 3945128224). Serviceable ELAC includes ELAC B L103+ (P/N 3945129117 or 3945128223) or any subsequent ELAC eligible for installation per Airbus instructions.

compliance_time: Before accumulating 22 years after THSA first flight, or within 3 months after 21 September 2012, whichever occurs later, and thereafter at intervals not exceeding 24 months for repetitive inspections. Corrective actions as defined in the Service Bulletin if corrosion is found.
required_action: Accomplish repetitive detailed inspections of the ballscrew lower splines of affected Trimmable Horizontal Stabilizer Actuators (THSA) to detect corrosion, and perform corrective actions (additional inspections and replacement) if corrosion is found. Do not install affected THSA parts unless they have not accumulated 22 years since first flight or are classified as Type 1 (no corrosion).
extraction_notes: Applicability is limited to aeroplanes with affected THSA parts installed (Group 1 aeroplanes). The affected parts are identified by Part Numbers listed in Appendix 1 of the AD. All manufacturer serial numbers are affected. The AD references Airbus Service Bulletin A320-27-1214 for inspection and corrective action procedures.

compliance_time: Within the threshold specified in Table 1 or Table 2 (whichever occurs later), and thereafter at intervals not exceeding 500 flight cycles or 1,000 flight hours (whichever occurs first) for repetitive detailed visual inspections; within the threshold specified in Table 3 for a one-time special detailed inspection of lug bore holes.
required_action: Perform repetitive detailed visual inspections of affected Main Landing Gear support rib 5 parts at specified intervals, and accomplish a one-time special detailed inspection of lug bore holes. If discrepancies are detected, contact Airbus for approved corrective instructions before next flight.
extraction_notes: Applicability is limited to specific aircraft serial numbers (MSN) listed in Appendix 1 of the AD. The affected parts are Main Landing Gear support rib 5 components with specific part numbers and serial numbers as detailed in Appendix 1. Compliance thresholds vary by aircraft series and are specified in Tables 1, 2, and 3.

compliance_time: Within 15 days after 28 July 2026 to determine rudder serial number; before exceeding 2,000 flight cycles or 12 months (whichever occurs first) since aeroplane reference date, or concurrently with first rudder removal after 28 July 2026 (whichever occurs first) to accomplish inspections; corrective actions within compliance time specified in the Service Bulletin if discrepancies are detected.
required_action: Visually inspect the rudder to determine its serial number; accomplish detailed visual inspection and woodpecker inspection of affected rudder areas in accordance with Airbus Service Bulletin A320-55-1070; perform corrective actions if discrepancies are detected; report rudder serial number and aeroplane MSN to Airbus within 15 days; report inspection results to Airbus within 30 days.
extraction_notes: This is Revision 01 of AD 2026-0144, issued to clarify compliance time for corrective actions. The applicability is limited to seven specific aircraft MSNs (12680, 12729, 12751, 12764, 12776, 12852, 12912) with specific rudder serial numbers listed in Appendix 1. Serial ranges are represented as individual serial numbers since only discrete MSNs are affected.

compliance_time: For Group 1 aeroplanes: within 4 months after 20 July 2026 for initial GVI, then at intervals not to exceed 4 months; within 24 months after 20 July 2026 for detailed inspection of battery support assemblies and replacement of affected parts. For Group 2 aeroplanes: from effective date, installation of affected parts allowed if new and identified with label within 24 months after 20 July 2026.
required_action: Identify and replace battery retaining rods (P/N D9241023700000) manufactured by SUDAERO or unknown supplier that have quality defects. Accomplish general visual inspections of affected parts at specified intervals, detailed inspection of battery support assemblies to identify manufacturer, and replace affected parts with serviceable parts or identify with label per Airbus service bulletins.
extraction_notes: The AD applies to all manufacturer serial numbers (MSN). Applicability is limited to specific aircraft models and variants as listed. The affected part is battery retaining rod P/N D9241023700000 manufactured by SUDAERO or unknown supplier, with specific exclusion criteria based on quality marking and supplier designation. Group 1 aeroplanes are those with affected parts installed (except those with Airbus modification 162321); Group 2 aeroplanes are all others. Compliance times reference 20 July 2026 as the effective date of the superseded AD 2026-0130.
